content.text: I've got the logging turned all the way up on a test of this, and I'm seeing some weird things from Jena's callbacks to JcrPropertyStatementListener.
While we look into that, let me reiterate some of what we discussed in
https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-2390,
that the WHERE clause is a pattern match, and that the redundant predicates don't mean what I think you're trying to imply. The attached is closer to what I think you want to accomplish.
I think we may need to take this up with Jena. Copying what I'm observing from logged interactions with the JcrPropertyStatementListener in IRC:

barmintor: awoods: ok
barmintor: awoods: I don't know what, but Jena is building up geometric solution sets when multiple patterns are present in a single update statement in Sparql-Update
barmintor: like modified statements m=2nv^n, where n is number of matching patterns and v is number of matched statements
barmintor: and it's more complicated with additional predicates
barmintor: but it's flat m=2v when there's only one predicate pattern in an update
barmintor: I guess that's "of course it's a flat m=2v", since there's only 1 pattern.
I'll try to correspond with
to see if we can get a suitable test demonstration together just in the Jena context. In the meantime,
please format your updates as we mentioned in the other ticket.
EDIT: The constant 2 in the function above was a log config error

To clarify, that is: Do not repeat predicate patterns, and if possible issue separate DELETE WHERE updates in the PATCH request entity. If what I'm seeing is right, having no repeated predicate patterns will result only in a number of messages equal to twice the matched statements. Those numbers explode if there is a duplicate predicate pattern.
has notes about the messages' origin in
FCREPO-2383

Barring changes to the ModelListener contract in Jena, Fedora is responsible for guaranteeing the uniqueness of the updates. I've opened a PR buffering them in a hash, but the committers should discuss the performance tradeoff here.
PR:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1169
Resolved with:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/0e62302ee1ee01f79ba177922852b007f8ce7c2b
This bug can be seen when executing a sparql-update request that attempts to delete a property several times.
The request hangs until an OOM exception is thrown.
The solution to this issue should be to return a 400 Bad Request.
To demonstrate the error:
Create a resource, "test".
> curl -i -XPUT localhost:8080/rest/test
Add properties to the new resource
> curl -i -XPATCH -H"Content-Type: application/sparql-update" --data-binary @rdf_insert.txt localhost:8080/rest/test
Attempt to delete resources
> curl -i -XPATCH -H"Content-Type: application/sparql-update" --data-binary @rdf_delete_duplicates.txt localhost:8080/rest/test
Notice request hangs
See attached "rdf_insert.txt" and "rdf_delete_one_multiple_one_non_existing.txt"
